title.value: Predicting Tactical Solutions to Operational Planning Problems under Imperfect Information
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the paper's focus on predicting tactical descriptions in operational planning using ML techniques, addressing the uncertainty in second-stage operational problems.
title.quote: This paper offers a methodological contribution at the intersection of machine learning and operations research. Namely, we propose a method- ology to quickly predict expected tactical descriptions of operational solu- tions (TDOSs).

extractions.description: The paper proposes a methodology to predict tactical descriptors of operational solutions under conditions of imperfect information by using supervised machine learning to approximate the solution of a stochastic optimal prediction problem. It applies this approach specifically to a load planning problem in rail transportation, demonstrating that the methodology can produce accurate high-speed predictions, thereby aiding quick decision-making in operational settings.

primary_category.justification: The paper contributes to optimizing operational planning in rail transportation, which is directly related to enhancing the efficiency of transportation systems—a key area in climate change mitigation.
primary_category.quote: We examine specifically the problem of predicting at high speed - in real time - with a trained ML approximator the expected TDOS pertaining to the railway container booking problem.

secondary_categories.justification: The specific details and applications do not extend directly to other eco-responsible AI categories beyond the primary transportation focus.
secondary_categories.quote: The problem is of practical importance and features characteristics that make it useful for illustrating the proposed methodology...

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper addresses operational planning in containerized rail transportation, seeking to optimize decisions on cargo capacity management—a sub-category of transportation under climate change mitigation.
primary_sub_category.quote: The first stage tactical problem consists in maximizing expected profit by controlling the accept/reject decision of a booking request for the transportation of a specified number of objects of standardized types on board available vehicles of standardized types.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No additional sub-categories from the eco-responsible AI list are directly addressed beyond the scope of transportation optimization discussed.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We considered an application related to railway demand and capacity management at the tactical level (accept / reject booking requests)...

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Despite detailed discussions of machine learning methodologies and optimization strategies, the focus remains prominently on transportation efficiency.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Namely, we aim to predict at a high speed the expected solution of the second stage problem, conditionally on the first stage variables.

applications.value: Optimizing freight routing and scheduling in rail transport
applications.justification: The paper illustrates the ML methodology applied to rail freight load planning, optimizing routing and scheduling decisions to increase efficiency.
applications.quote: As a motivating application, we consider a myopic, two-stage booking control problem pertaining to cargo capacity management.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper fits within existing eco-responsible AI categories under 'Climate Change Mitigation' and related sub-categories, primarily Transportation.
new_primary_category.quote: We examine specifically the problem of predicting at high speed... by avoiding the online generation of multiple second stage scenarios and solutions.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not require a new sub-category beyond existing classifications as it clearly aligns with 'Transportation' within 'Climate Change Mitigation.'
new_primary_sub_category.quote: This may be used in support of the solution to the overall two-stage problem by avoiding the online generation of multiple second stage scenarios and solutions.
